literature.question: Is there a published rule for how far apart two duplexes protruding from one origami face must sit?
literature.answer: NOT FOUND. C-0037's own ~72 queries and C-0028's and C-0029's ~110 before it found no published spacing rule; this task's queries add to that and change nothing.

literature.question: How many spacers does the literature's only rigid out-of-plane mounting have, and does the paper say how they are arranged?
literature.answer: EXACTLY TWO, each 39 bp, one covalent link per end — and the paper does NOT say how they are arranged: the word 'spacer' occurs twice in the whole article. So there is no published precedent to agree or disagree with this task's separation.
literature.flag: read directly, via C-0037 which fetched and counted the SI strand table
literature.source: Pumm et al., Nature 607:492, EuropePMC PMC9300469

literature.question: The intrastrand phosphodiester step the closure test is written on
literature.answer: A WINDOW, 0.60-0.70 nm: 'C3-endo (interphosphate distance 0.6 nm) to C2-endo conformation (interphosphate distance 0.7 nm)'.

literature.question: The phosphate radius the counting theorem rests on
literature.answer: 'Phosphates (red circles) sit at a radius of a_DNA = 10 A' — which IS the duplex's own steric radius.
literature.source: Hedley, Coshic, Aksimentiev & Kornyshev, Phys. Rev. X 14:031042 (2024)

literature.question: Has a torsion-level check of any 90 degree scaffold excursion been published?
literature.answer: NOT FOUND, and it is this project's own T-71. This task inherits C-0029's caveat unchanged: the closure test is NECESSARY and never sufficient.

findings.verdict: The pair FITS. At every separation from the 6 bp steric floor upward a second standoff seats on the same sheet duplex with both links inside the measured [0.60, 0.70] nm step and zero unpaired nucleotides, and the best pair at 7 bp holds its worse chord 0.00 deg off the flexure axis, i.e. 1.0000 of the base couple still lands in the loaded plane.
findings.the cheap bound that did not bind: If the second junction were the first one's SCREW IMAGE its chord would be rotated by n x 33.74 deg, which at C-0037's recommended 8 bp is 89.9 deg — the entire couple moved onto the wrong plane, and 8 bp would be the single worst separation in the band. It does not bind, because a standoff must stand NORMAL to the sheet and a screw rotation about a horizontal axis does not preserve that: the second standoff's own azimuth and axial position are free and it reaches a different target pair. That freedom is the whole answer.
findings.what it costs in azimuth: NOTHING, at every separation from 6 to 12 bp, on both groove conventions, on the strict seat-duplex-only reading and at the seat duplex's own axis: both chords come out EXACTLY on the flexure axis, so C-0037's best-phase assumption is discharged rather than merely noted. The one cost anywhere in the sweep is the scaffold-excursion topology at 6 and 9 bp, worth 3.13 and 5.87 deg, i.e. 0.30 % and 1.04 % of the couple — against C-0037's own 8.4 % allowance.
findings.the separation is NOT free, and 7 bp is: C-0037 reports 6, 8 and 12 bp as bit-identical and recommends 8. They are identical in the LOADED plane, and this task reproduces that exactly; they are not identical in the FREE one, which is the plane C-0037's own truss was built to restrain. At 6 bp the free plane still governs at 8.84 pN (margin 2.52); at 7 bp it has crossed and the loaded plane governs at 9.77 pN (margin 2.79), which is C-0037's L2a8 number. So SEVEN base pairs buys the whole of the recommended design at 0.68 nm less row width, and C-0037's 'between 6 and 8 bp' is resolved to 7.
findings.why 7 bp in particular: Because the second standoff has two moves the screw image does not: a swap to the seat duplex's OTHER backbone, worth +/-120 deg, and a half turn about its own axis, which is free because a chord is a LINE. The sheet phase residual under those moves is 3.8 deg at 7 bp against 22.4 at 6 and 29.9 at 8 — and at 7 bp the search's two standoffs duly come out as literal translates at ONE azimuth (300.0 deg), one grounded on each backbone of the same duplex. It is an explanation and not a bound: at 6 and 11 bp the two standoffs come out a half turn apart instead, and the alignment is still exact.
findings.the seat is a bound, not an output: An unbounded search parks the optimum on the RIM of the seat duplex, where the flat end face's line contact 2 sqrt(R^2 - y^2) has collapsed to a point and the standoff is balanced on an edge. The seats swept here keep that contact above 1.6 nm; the wider sweep is carried as a sensitivity.
findings.what is NOT shown: A NECESSARY condition only — a phosphate pair inside the measured step with no van der Waals overlap. No backbone torsion angle is checked and no sequence is designed, so a 'closes' verdict is an UPPER bound on buildability. T-71 is the check that can only make it worse, and it now has two junctions to check instead of one.
